title: Jason Calacanis: from Brooklyn grit to Silicon Alley Reporter, Weblogs Inc and All-In
summary: Jason tells how a Brooklyn kid with no money built Silicon Alley Reporter from a photocopied zine, lost it in the dotcom bust, then rebuilt with Weblogs Inc and sold to AOL for $30M. He also covers moderating All-In, loyalty in friendships, and defining success as enthusiasm rather than net worth.

principles.text: Get to a new medium first; early movers collect disproportionate credit and value.
principles.quote: I was always very interested in mediums right because if you get to a medium first you can exploit it

principles.text: Ask for things, even outrageous ones; people often say yes.
principles.quote: when I ask people things that many times people will do what I ask them to do

principles.text: Use rejection as fuel to prove it was no fluke, and start building the very next day.
principles.quote: I am going to prove I can do this again I am going to show everybody that this was not a fluke

principles.text: After a crash, call around the ecosystem to see what builders are tinkering with and spot the next wave.
principles.quote: I started calling people up I started calling people out what are you working on what's happening

principles.text: Model unit economics in a spreadsheet, then scale the content business and someone will buy it.
principles.quote: all we have to do with this business is scale it and then somebody will buy it

principles.text: Judge success by whether you can't wait to get out of bed, and design your life around that.
principles.quote: the right score card is did you wake up and couldn't get couldn't wait to get out of bed
